visual_action: A woman, Adelita Grijalva, speaks directly to the camera in what appears to be an office. Behind her are several posters, including one that reads "PROTECT OAK FLAT!" and "APACHE STRONG". Throughout her speech, text overlays appear on screen, summarizing her points. At the end, a yellow banner with a URL is shown.

cast.name: Adelita Grijalva
cast.evidence: She is the sole speaker in the video, identified by face-ID, and is talking about her own situation of not being sworn into Congress.

cast.name: Mike Johnson
cast.evidence: He is repeatedly named as the person preventing Grijalva from being sworn in. She says, "Speaker Johnson continues to make excuses." The caption also names him.

spoken_summary: Adelita Grijalva states that she was elected to Congress two weeks ago but has not been sworn in because Speaker Johnson is making excuses and refusing to do so, leaving Southern Arizona without a voice in Washington. She recounts that Johnson first cited certification, then whether Congress was in session, and that they "won't even end their vacations to come to work." She claims Johnson promised to swear her in "whenever I wanted" but then walked it back. She asks her supporters to sign a petition at adelita.us/sign and to continue applying pressure to get her sworn in.
audio_music: The audio consists solely of a woman's voice speaking directly to the camera. There is no background music or other sound effects.
editing_pacing: The video is a static, single-shot talking head. The main editing consists of frequent text overlays that appear sequentially to emphasize the speaker's words.
central_claim: Republican Speaker Mike Johnson is illegitimately refusing to swear in the democratically elected Adelita Grijalva, disenfranchising her constituents in Southern Arizona.
intended_effect: To mobilize supporters to pressure Speaker Johnson by signing a petition and to generate outrage at Republicans for what is portrayed as an anti-democratic action.
